Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:33: Further, they explained several things concerning the matter of "with the measure a person measures, so he is measured," and I will copy some of them, not all, so as not to lengthen. We have learned in the Mishnah (Sotah 1:7): with the measure a person measures, so he is measured - she adorned herself for transgression, the Omnipresent disfigured her; she exposed herself for transgression, the Omnipresent exposed her. The thigh began the transgression first and afterward the belly, therefore the thigh was struck first and afterward the belly, and the rest of the body did not escape. Samson went after his eyes, therefore the Philistines gouged out his eyes, as it is said (Judges 16:21), "and the Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes." Absalom took pride in his hair, therefore he was hanged by his hair; and because he came upon his father's ten concubines, therefore ten young men thrust [spears] into him, as it is said (II Samuel 18:15), "and ten young men who bore Joab's armor surrounded him." And because he stole three hearts - his father's heart, the court's heart, and Israel's heart, as it is said (ibid. 15:6), "and Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel" - therefore three darts were thrust into him, as it is said (ibid. 18:14), "and he took three darts in his hand and thrust them into Absalom's heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:34: And so too regarding good: Miriam waited for Moses one hour, as it is said (Exodus 2:4), "and his sister stood at a distance" - therefore Israel was delayed for her seven days in the wilderness, as it is said (Numbers 12:15), "and the people did not journey until Miriam was gathered in." Joseph merited to bury his father, and none of his brothers was greater than he, as it is said (Genesis 50:9), "and Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went up both chariots and horsemen" - who is greater to us than Joseph, whom none but Moses attended to? Moses merited [to attend to] Joseph's bones, and none in Israel was greater than he, as it is said (Exodus 13:19), "and Moses took the bones of Joseph with him" - who is greater to us than Moses, whom none but the Omnipresent attended to, as it is said (Deuteronomy 34:6), "and He buried him in the valley"? And this was said not of Moses alone, but of all the righteous, as it is said (Isaiah 58:8), "and your righteousness shall go before you, the glory of the LORD shall gather you" - to this point. And they further elaborated on similar matters in the Tosefta of Sotah, chapter 3; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:35: And in the Gemara (Sotah 8b) it is taught there: it was taught, Rabbi Meir would say, with the measure a person measures, so he is measured, as it is said (Isaiah 27:8), "in full measure, when You send her away, You contend with her" - I know only a se'ah [a full measure]; Rashi explains: a great transgression. From where do we include a tarkav and half a tarkav, a kav and half a kav, a quarter-kav and half a quarter-kav, an eighth and a sixteenth? The verse teaches (ibid. 9:4), "for every boot of the tramping warrior." And from where do we know that every single peruta [small coin] combines into a large sum? The verse teaches, "one to one, to find the sum" - to this point. And Rashi explains: "from where that every single peruta," etc. - even though he was not punished for the first and second [transgressions], they were not forgiven him; rather, they are combined for him into the [final] reckoning - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:36: Further, it is said in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Zuta, chapter 3): the Holy One, blessed be He, created everything in His world except for the attribute of falsehood and the attribute of injustice, as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:4), "the Rock, His work is perfect," and so on; (Zephaniah 3:5), "the LORD is righteous within her, He does no injustice"; and it says (Job 34:10), "far be it from God to do wickedness," and so on, "for the work of a man He will render to him." I call heaven and earth to witness for me: no creature descends into suffering except from the fact that he eats and drinks and rejoices, he and his wife and his children and all that is his, and [then] departs to his eternal home.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:37: Fruits and grain do not come to rot except from people's [bad] ways; people's eyes do not dim in the middle of their days except from their ways; people are not defiled with plagues except from their ways; people do not come to a foul odor except from their ways; and women are not defiled with a flow except from their ways, as it is said (Isaiah 45:18), "so says the LORD, the Creator of the heavens, He is God." Go and learn from the way of the world: does a person build a house except in order to bring vessels into it and bring produce into it? So too, people are judged according to their ways, in order to save them from the day that is coming.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:38: And not only that, but a person considers three things every day: when he enters the privy, [an inner voice] tells him, see your way is rotten [maggot-ridden]; when he lets blood, it tells him, you are flesh and blood; when he walks before the dead, it tells him, see before whom you are walking. And still he does not repent, and speaks excessive words, as it is said (Proverbs 19:3), "the foolishness of man perverts his way." If a person makes himself devoted to truth, he is given an angel who conducts himself with him in the way of the righteous and speaks truth; if a person makes himself wicked, given to divination and falsehood, he is given an angel who conducts himself with him in the way of the wicked and practices divination and falsehood. If a person makes himself pious, to bear everything, he is given an angel who conducts himself with him in the way of the pious and bears everything, as it is said (Jeremiah 17:10), "I the LORD search the heart," and so on, "to give to each man according to his ways," and so on. And so too of David it says (Psalms 18:27), "with the pure You show Yourself pure"; and it says (ibid. 18:28), "for You save the afflicted people" - for poverty befits him - "but haughty eyes You bring low" - these are the wicked of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:39: And so too it is further said in the Mechilta, on the verse (Exodus 19:1), "in the third month after the children of Israel went out of the land of Egypt" - in these words: this teaches that they counted months from the exodus from Egypt. I know only months - from where [do we know they counted] years? The verse teaches, "in the second year," and so on. And it says afterward: I know only [that they counted] until the Temple was built - from where [do we know they counted] after the Temple was built? The verse teaches (I Kings 6:1), "and it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year... that he began to build the house" [cross-reference variant], "and it was at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built" [I Kings 9:10]. They did not want to count for its building, so they count for its destruction, as it is said (Ezekiel 40:1), "after the city was struck." They did not want to count for themselves, so they count for others, as it is said (Haggai 1:1), "in the second year of Darius" - "in the second year of Nebuchadnezzar" (cf. Daniel 2:1). And so it says (Song of Songs 1:8), "if you do not know, O fairest among women," and so on; and so it says (Deuteronomy 28:47), "because you did not serve" - you did not want to be subjugated to Heaven, so you are subjugated before the nations. You did not want to weigh the shekels of Heaven, a beka per head, so you weigh fifteen shekels in the kingdom of your enemies. You did not want to repair the roads and streets for the pilgrims to the Chosen House, so you repair the watch-posts on the roads leading up to the cities of kings. And so it says (Deuteronomy 28:47-48), "because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart, out of the abundance of everything, therefore you shall serve your enemy" - in hatred. Because you did not serve the LORD your God with drink, you shall serve your enemy in thirst. Because you did not serve the LORD your God clothed, you shall serve your enemy in nakedness. Because you did not serve the LORD your God out of the abundance of everything, you shall serve your enemy in the lack of everything - what is "the lack of everything"? That understanding was taken from them, and [they were left] lacking Torah - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:40: Further, one must fear, for the Holy One, blessed be He, did several things in the world in order to arouse a person to fear before Him, blessed be He, and not sin - along the lines of what our Sages, of blessed memory, said on (Ecclesiastes 3:14), "and God has done it, that men should fear before Him" (Berachot 55a): Rabbah bar bar Chanah said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: this refers to a bad dream. Rabbi Alexandri said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: thunder was created only to straighten the crookedness of the heart, as it is said, "and God has done it, that men should fear before Him" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:41: And in Parashat Pinchas (239b) it is explained there that "God" [Elohim] refers to Gevurah, [and the meaning is that He] did this within the Shechinah, that they should fear before Him, since the Shechinah is the place of judgment. In these words: "what is 'God has done'? Another tree below Him, and He does not do it in this one - for this lower tree does it and establishes it; and whoever enters the upper tree enters by permission, and should forget the lower tree and fear to enter it, but rather as is fitting. Come and see, this [lower tree] is the guardian of the gate, and therefore it is called 'the Guardian of Israel,' and this lower tree is watered and nourished from the tree above; and therefore it is not written 'will do' but 'has done' - why, that the people of the world should fear before Him and not approach Him except those fit to approach, and no other - so that people should guard the ways of the Torah and not turn to the right or to the left" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:42: And he explained two things about fear: the first, that one who is unfit should not approach the holy, for not everyone who wishes to take the Name may take it - as I explained in the Introduction in the name of Rashbi, from Parashat Naso, that one who wishes to come to the holy has many accusers against him if he is unfit, and this is comparable to one who wishes to enter to see the king's face - before he enters to see the king, how many gates within gates there are, and how many officers are appointed at every single gate.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:43: And the second, "that people should guard the ways of the Torah," and so on - and this is as explained in the Zohar, Parashat Vayetze (152a): "and they put the stone back over the mouth of the well, in its place" - referring to the saying about the well, similar to "by the mouth of the LORD they encamped" - meaning that it needs a stumbling-stone and a rock of offense to chastise people.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:44: And by this matter a bad dream and thunder may be understood, for they are all forces of judgment spreading from it [the Shechinah] to chastise people; and when the Holy One, blessed be He, chastises a person with sufferings, he is obligated to submit to the judgment that rules over him, and not stiffen his neck, and not kick against the sufferings. And if he hardens his heart, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Genesis 12:1) that of him it is said (Proverbs 28:14), "and he who hardens his heart shall fall into evil" - which is the external [husk] - therefore one must fear Him, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:45: And he should consider what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in the Tanchuma (Tazria 8), on the verse (Habakkuk 1:7), "he is terrible and awesome; his justice and his dignity proceed from himself" - in these words, in the Yalkut on Habakkuk: another interpretation, "he is terrible and awesome" - this is man, who rules over everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created, as it is written (Psalms 8:7), "You have made him rule over the works of Your hands." "His justice and his dignity proceed from himself" - when he sins, the Holy One, blessed be He, brings sufferings upon him from his own body. A king of flesh and blood, when he chastises his servants, brings whips and ropes and chastises them; but the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so - when He wishes to chastise a person, He chastises him from the person's own body, as it is said (Leviticus 13:2), "when a man shall have in the skin of his flesh," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:46: Further, when a person considers the roar of the lion, of which everyone is afraid, as it is written (Amos 3:8), "the lion has roared, who will not fear?" - how much more so should he fear Him, blessed be He, as it is written (Jeremiah 10:10), "but the LORD is the true God, He is the living God and the eternal King; at His wrath the earth trembles, and the nations cannot endure His indignation." And so they said in the Midrash on Proverbs (chapter 20), on the verse (Proverbs 20:2), "the fear of a king is like the roaring of a lion" - in these words: Rabbi Yehuda bar Simon said, these thunders, when they go forth, shake the whole world, and the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, is how much more so! Another interpretation: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said, just as when this young lion cries out with its voice, one who hears it is afraid - how much more so the roar of the Holy One, blessed be He! - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:47: Further, he should fear, for the Holy One, blessed be He, has many agents to execute judgment upon people to collect His debt. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Bereshit Rabbah (10:5), on the verse (Job 7:1), "is there not a hard service for man on earth?" - in these words: the Holy One, blessed be He, appointed many armies against man to demand satisfaction for His insult - many bears, many lions, many snakes, many scorpions; and not only that, but even like the days of a hired laborer. The Rabbis say: even things that you regard as though they were superfluous to the creation of the world, such as gnats, fleas, and flies - even they are included in the creation of the world, and in all of it the Holy One, blessed be He, performs His mission, even through a scorpion, even through a gnat, even through a frog - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:48: Further, they explained, of blessed memory, in the Yelammedenu, that the Kutim [Samaritans/gentile nations] too are agents to cause harm when Israel does not do the will of the Omnipresent; and in these words, on the verse (Micah 7:16), "the nations shall see and be ashamed," and so on, "they shall lick the dust like a serpent" - when you do not do My will, just as the serpent was incited against Adam and Eve to destroy them from the world, so I incite against you the Kutim, who are likened to serpents, as it is said (Jeremiah 46:22), "her voice goes like a serpent"; and so it says (Ecclesiastes 10:11), "if the serpent bites without being charmed" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:49: And so too they explained in the Zohar, Parashat Shemini (36b), that the Kutim and all the beasts of the field are all agents to cause harm; in these words: how many agents the Holy One, blessed be He, has, and through all of them He performs His mission, even through wild beasts - as it is written (Leviticus 26:22), "and I will send the beast of the field against you, and it shall bereave you"; and even through the hand of another nation, as it is written (Deuteronomy 28:49), "the LORD will bring a nation against you from afar, from the end of the earth." Rabbi Elazar said: and through the hand of Israel too He performs His mission. He said to him: yes, such as a wicked man through the hand of a righteous man - meaning that the righteous man is commanded to flog the wicked man, as it is said (ibid. 25:2), "and it shall be, if the wicked man deserves to be beaten," and so on. He said further: but a wicked man through the hand of another wicked Israelite - He does not perform His mission through him except at a time when he does not intend it [i.e., accidentally] - as it is written (Exodus 21:13), "and he did not lie in wait, but God caused it to come to his hand." "And he did not lie in wait" - precisely, that he did not intend to kill him, but "God caused it to come to his hand," in order to punish both of them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:50: And they explained there the reason: that the wicked and the beasts of the field come from the left side, and at a time when people do not prepare their deeds properly, these are a strap to flog them - for since they transgressed the Torah, they are marked, and the agents of judgment recognize them. However, one Israelite through the hand of another Israelite - even though he is wicked - is still, after all, on the right side, and is not an agent; rather, guilt is rolled about through a guilty party, so that both may be punished.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 11:51: Of this category of fear is what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Sotah 8b): Rabbi Chiya taught: from the day the Temple was destroyed, even though the four death penalties [of the court] were abolished, the law of the four death penalties was not abolished. One who was liable for stoning either falls from a roof or a beast tramples him; one who was liable for burning either falls into a fire or a snake bites him; one who was liable for beheading is either handed over to the [gentile] government or robbers come upon him; one who was liable for strangulation either drowns in a river or dies of croup [quinsy] - and so too regarding a good measure [reward] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:1: In explaining the fear stemming from death and the other matters attached to it - our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Shabbat 31b), explained that the wicked are not anxious about the day of death; in these words, on "for there are no torments in their death" (Psalms 73:4): Rabbah bar Ulla expounded: the Holy One, blessed be He, said, it is not enough for the wicked that they are not anxious and grieved about the day of death, but their heart is as sound to them as a [banquet] hall - to this point. It appears that one must fear the day of death so as to prepare provisions to go to his eternal home, as King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Ecclesiastes 7:4), "the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:2: And so too in the Zohar (Vayechi 227a) they called the day of death "the day of the great judgment," on which a person is judged for all his deeds. In these words: Rabbi Chizkiyah opened and said (Genesis 15:12), "and it came to pass, as the sun was about to set, that a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and behold, a great dark dread fell upon him" - this is the harsh day of judgment that takes a person out of this world; for it is taught, on the day a person departs from this world, that day is the day of the great judgment, when the sun is darkened from the moon, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 12:2), "before the sun grows dark" - this is the holy soul, which is withheld from a person thirty days before he departs the world; and this is the tzelem [image/shadow] that is withheld from him and is not seen. Why is it withheld from him? Because the holy soul ascends and departs from him and is not seen - lest you say that only when a person dies and weakens does this soul depart from him; rather, while he is yet in his strength, in his lifetime, this soul departs, and it does not illuminate the spirit, and the spirit does not illuminate the [animal] soul - then the tzelem departs from him and does not shine upon him. And from that day, everything proclaims about him, even the birds of heaven - why? Because the soul has already ascended from him, and the spirit does not illuminate the [animal] soul; then the [animal] soul weakens, and all appetite for food and all bodily desire departs and ceases from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:3: And Rabbi Yehuda said: even the whole time a person falls into his sickbed and cannot pray, the soul has departed and ascended from him, and then the spirit does not illuminate the [animal] soul until the person's judgment is decided; and if they judge the person favorably, then the soul returns to its place and illuminates everything - to this point. It is explained in this passage that thirty days before his death, the soul and the tzelem depart from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:4: And so too it is further explained there, in the passage above this one (217b), in these words: Rabbi Yosi said, when that person's days draw near, thirty days [before death] it is proclaimed about him in the world, and even the birds of heaven proclaim about him; and if he is righteous, thirty days it is proclaimed about him among the righteous in the Garden of Eden. We have learned: all those thirty days, his soul goes out from him every night and ascends and sees its place in that world, and that person does not know and does not notice and has no control over his soul all those thirty days, as it was originally, as it is written (Ecclesiastes 8:8), "no man has power over the spirit, to restrain the spirit." Rabbi Yehuda said: from when those thirty days remain, the person's tzelem darkens, and the image that used to be seen on earth is withheld - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:5: And in Parashat Vayikra (Zohar 13a) they explained that there are two tzelamim [images], one large and one small, and both are upon a person, and of them it is said (Song of Songs 2:17), "until the day breathes and the shadows flee," and so on - and we copied the passage in chapter 4; see there. And it says there concerning "until the day breathes": until the day of this world breathes its last, and that mighty day comes when the King demands judgment of it, to go out from this world, and so on, "to return before its Master." Behold, they called the day of death the day of judgment, and one must fear it in order to correct his deeds before his day comes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:6: And so too it is further explained in the Zohar (Vayechi 218b): it is taught, on that mighty and fearsome day when a person's time comes to depart from the world, the four sides of the world stand in harsh judgment, and judgments are aroused from the four sides of the world, and four bonds go forth, and strife is found among them, and each must separate to its own side. A herald goes out to each side and proclaims in that world, and it is heard in two hundred seventy worlds: if he is righteous, all the worlds rejoice to greet him; and if not, woe to that person and to his portion.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:7: It is taught, at the time the herald proclaims, then a flame goes forth from the north side and goes and is kindled in the River of Fire and separates to the four sides of the world, and burns the souls of the wicked; and that flame goes out and ascends and descends in the world, and that flame reaches the wings of a black rooster and strikes its wings and calls out at the gate between the doors. The first time it calls out and says (Malachi 3:19), "for behold, the day comes, burning like a furnace," and so on. The second time it calls out and says (Amos 4:13), "for behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what is his thought" - and at that hour the person sits with his witnessing deeds before him, and he confesses concerning them. The third time, when they wish to take his soul out from him, the rooster calls out and says (Jeremiah 10:7), "who would not fear You, King of the nations? For it befits You."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:8: Rabbi Yosi said: the black rooster - for what purpose does it go forth? Rabbi Yehuda said: everything the Holy One, blessed be He, did on earth is all hinted at in wisdom, except that people do not know it - as it is written (Psalms 104:24), "how many are Your works, O LORD! You have made them all in wisdom," and so on; and since they were all made in wisdom, they are all hinted at in wisdom. And [as for] the black rooster - we have learned, judgment rests only in a place of its own kind, and black comes from the side of judgment; and therefore precisely at midnight, when the spirit of the north side is aroused, a flame goes forth and strikes beneath the rooster's wings and it calls out - and all the more so a black rooster, which is more attuned than another. Here too, at the hour of a person's judgment, [that flame] is aroused and calls to him, and none knows it but that dying person - for we have learned, at the hour a person lies dying and judgment rests upon him to depart from this world, a supernal spirit is added to him that was not in him during his lifetime, and once it rests upon him and clings to him, he sees what he did not merit to see in his lifetime, because that spirit was added to him; and when it is added to him and he sees, then he departs from this world - as it is written (ibid. 104:29), "when You take away their spirit, they perish, and return to their dust" - then it is written (Exodus 33:20), "for man shall not see Me and live" - in their lives they do not merit [to see], in their death they merit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:9: It is taught, at the hour a person dies, permission is given him to see, and he sees near him his relatives and companions from that world and recognizes them, and they are all engraved in their images as they were in this world. If that person is righteous, they all rejoice before him and greet him with peace; and if he is not righteous, none are recognized near him except those wicked ones who torment them daily in Gehinnom, and they are all sorrowful and open with "woe" and end with "woe," and he lifts his eyes and sees them like a spark rising from a fire - so too he opens with "woe."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:10: It is taught, at the hour a person's soul departs, all his relatives and companions from that world go with his soul and show him the place of delight and the place of punishment. If he is righteous, he sees his place and ascends and sits and delights in the supernal delight of that world; and if he is not righteous, that soul remains in this world until the body is hidden in the earth. Once it is hidden, several officers of the [heavenly] laws seize it until it reaches Dumah [the angel of the grave], and they bring it into its dwelling in Gehinnom.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:11: Rav Yehuda said: for all seven days [after burial] the soul goes from its house to its grave and from its grave to its house, and mourns over the body, as it is written (Job 14:22), "but his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn." It goes and sits in its house, sees them all sorrowful and mourning. It is taught: after the seven days, the body becomes as it was [decomposing], and the soul enters its place - it enters the Cave of Machpelah, and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:12: Further, it is explained concerning the matters of a person's departure from this world (Lech Lecha 78b), in these words: Rabbi Elazar said, happy are the righteous who learn the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, in order to walk in them and to fear Him from that day of judgment when a person is destined to give judgment and reckoning to the Holy One, blessed be He. He opened and said (Job 37:7), "He seals the hand of every man, that all men may know His work" - this verse has been established [elsewhere], but come and see: on that day when a person's days are completed to depart from the world, that day when the body breaks and the soul wishes to separate from it, then permission is given to the person to see what he did not have permission to see while the body ruled and stood in its full strength; and then three agents stand over him and reckon his days and his sins and everything he did in this world, and he confesses to all of it with his mouth, and afterward he seals it with his own hand - this is "He seals the hand of every man" - and by his hand all is sealed, to judge him in that world for the first and for the last, for the new and for the old; not one of them is forgotten - this is "that all men may know His work." And all those deeds he did in this world in body and spirit, so too he gives account in body and spirit before he departs the world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:13: Further, all the details of departure are explained in the Zohar (Naso 126a), in these words: Rabbi Abba opened (Psalms 103:1), "of David, bless the LORD, O my soul, and all that is within me, bless His holy name" - how much a person must contemplate and know about the service of his Master! For every single day a herald calls out and says (Proverbs 1:22), "how long, simple ones, will you love simplicity? Return, wayward children, I will heal your backslidings" (Jeremiah 3:22), and there is none who inclines his ear; the Torah proclaims before them and there is none who pays heed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:14: Come and see, a person goes about in this world and thinks that it is his forever, and that he will remain within it for generations upon generations; but while he goes about in the world, they place a collar upon him, and while he sits, they judge him in fetters together with the rest of those under judgment. If he is found to have a defender, he is saved from judgment - this is (Job 33:23), "if there be for him an angel, an intercessor, one out of a thousand, to declare to man his uprightness, then He is gracious to him and says," and so on. And who is the defender? Those proper deeds that stand for the person at the time he needs them; and if no defender is found for him, he is condemned by the judgment to depart from the world. At that hour, when he lies fettered by the King's collar, until he lifts his eyes and sees two [agents] coming to him who write before him everything he did in this world and everything that came out of his mouth, and judgment is passed on all of it, and it is written before him - this is (Amos 4:13), "for behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what is his thought," and so on - and he confesses to them. Why? Because that deed which he did rises and stands over him to testify against him, and they stand to testify against him, and they all descend and are recorded before him, and stand before him, and do not depart from him until the hour he is judged for them in that world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:15: Come and see, all those words a person does in this world are all prepared before him and are not lost from him; and at the hour they take him out to the grave, they all present themselves before him, and three heralds proclaim - one before him, one on his right, and one on his left - and they say: this is so-and-so who rebelled against his Master, rebelled above, rebelled below, rebelled against the Torah, rebelled against its commandments - see his deeds, see his words, better for him that he had not been created. By the time he reaches the grave, all the dead are aroused from their places against him and say, woe that this one is buried among us - his deeds and his words go ahead and enter the grave and stand over that body, and his spirit goes and wanders and mourns over the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:16: Once a person is hidden in the grave, Dumah comes forth in advance, and under his hand are three courts appointed over the judgment of the grave, and three fiery rods in their hands, and they judge spirit and body together. Woe over that judgment, woe over his deeds, at the hour he is seized by the King's collar and his judgment is decided and completed, that no defender was found for him - the King's guard descends and stands before him, at his feet, with a sharpened sword in his hand. The person lifts his eyes and sees the walls of the house ablaze with fire from his radiance; meanwhile he sees before him one full of eyes, his garments a blazing fire, before the person - so it is indeed, for how many people have seen an angel in the marketplace standing before them, while the rest of the people do not see him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:17: And should you say, is it not written (Psalms 104:4), "He makes His angels winds," and so on - how can [an angel] appear on earth? Rather, this matter has been established: once he descends, he clothes himself in a body and appears to whoever it appears to, in that garment in which he is clothed; and if not, the world could not bear it nor could it appear - how much more so this one [the angel of death], whom all the people of the world need. Three drops on his sword, and so on - and the colleagues have established this: once [the dying person] sees him, his whole body and spirit tremble, and his heart does not settle, because he [the angel] is the king of the whole body, and his spirit goes through all the limbs of the body and is drawn out from them like a person drawn away by his companion to go to another place. Then he says, woe over what he did - and nothing helps him except if the remedy of repentance comes first, before that hour arrives. The person is afraid and wishes to hide and cannot; once he sees that he cannot, he opens his eyes and must gaze upon him, and gazes upon him with open eyes; and then he removes his own body and soul, and that hour is the time of the great judgment by which a person is judged in this world. And with all this, the spirit goes and wanders through all the limbs and trembles on every side, and all the limbs of the body all tremble; when the spirit reaches each and every limb and is drawn out from it, a shudder falls upon that limb and the spirit ascends from it and that limb immediately dies, and so with all of them. Once the spirit reaches the point of departing, having been drawn out from the body, then the Shechinah stands over him and immediately it flies from the body. Happy is the portion of one who cleaves to it; woe to those who are far from it and do not cleave to it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:18: And through several courts a person passes when he departs from this world: one, that supernal judgment we mentioned, when the spirit goes out from the body; and one judgment, when his deeds and his words go before him and heralds proclaim about him; and one judgment, when he enters the grave; and the judgment of the grave; and one judgment of the worm; and one judgment of Gehinnom; and one judgment of the spirit that goes and wanders in the world and finds no place until his deeds are completed - certainly seven periods pass over him. Therefore, while a person is found in this world, he must fear his Master and contemplate, every single day, his own deeds, and repent of them before his Master.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:19: When King David contemplated those judgments of a person when he departs from this world, he said in advance (Psalms 104:1), "bless the LORD, O my soul" - before you depart from the world, now that you are found together with the body; "and all that is within me, [bless] His holy name" - you limbs that partner with the spirit, now that you are found with it, hasten to bless the holy Name before the time comes when you will no longer be able to bless Him and give thanks concerning yourselves - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 12:20: It was said in a baraita (Avodah Zarah 20b): they said of the Angel of Death that he is full of eyes all over; at the time of a sick person's departure, he stands over his head with his sword drawn in his hand, and a drop of gall hangs from it. Once the sick person sees him, he trembles and opens his mouth, and it [the drop] is cast into his mouth; from it he dies, from it he decomposes, from it his face turns green. And we say further there in the Gemara: the Master said, "from it he dies" - shall we say this disputes the father of Shmuel, for the father of Shmuel said, the Angel of Death told me: were it not that I am concerned for the honor of humanity, I would tear open the place of slaughter [the throat] like an animal? Perhaps that drop cuts the [vital] organs. And Rashi explains: thus it is indeed a literal cutting - perhaps that drop cuts the organs - to this point.
